title: PTP random variable represented as packet Mirror code
hypothesis: A single packet address, read through phase-specific low-description Mirror views, can generate a jointly consistent P=4 trajectory when branch uncertainty is shared across phases; when branch entropy is independent per phase, the required address entropy grows from one to four bits. Mirror must be compared with a simple shared-code embedding and PTP per-slot auxiliaries so any gain is attributed to the view rather than the compact address alone.
physical_object: one shared phase-slot decoder plus one packet-address embedding table
mirror_coordinate: one categorical packet code, transformed by a learned phase-specific Givens rotation before each logical slot reads it
logical_multiplicity: four phase-specific next-state functions from one shared packet address and decoder
teacher: P=4 transitions through two random state-permutation tables; correlated world draws one branch bit for the entire packet, independent world draws one bit per phase

task.metric: per-token NLL, exact joint packet accuracy, valid-path rate

controls: shared categorical packet embedding broadcast to every phase
shared packet embedding with scalar phase gates
shared packet code with phase-specific Givens Mirror views
untied per-phase packet-code embeddings as a capacity upper control

development.selection_metric: mean validation token NLL across methods and both source modes

storage.authority: actual serialized model payload bytes plus per-packet random-address bits, reported separately and summed for the per-packet frontier
storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON
paid_objects: all Givens angles or scalar gates

success_gate: In all three fresh correlated worlds, Mirror exact joint packet accuracy >=99%, per-token NLL <=1.10x PTP and valid path >=99%; its address entropy must not exceed the PTP source entropy (1 bit correlated, 4 bits independent). A Mirror-specific improvement additionally requires a better model-payload/quality point than both broadcast and scalar-gate controls. Independent-mode result maps the entropy boundary.
failure_gate: In all three fresh correlated worlds, Mirror quality misses the PTP gate, or broadcast/scalar-gate matches quality with equal or fewer model bytes. If quality passes but no Mirror-specific frontier gain exists, classify the mechanism as feasible but not Mirror-specific. Independent-mode quality/address failure alone maps the entropy boundary.
boundaries: not a general claim that one packet code can replace independent auxiliaries
fixed-update mechanism screen rather than near-convergence capacity study
PTP random auxiliary is discretized to the teacher's binary branch choice

protocol_amendments.stage: development only; no fresh worlds opened
protocol_amendments.reason: The initial one-block development pass produced low joint packet accuracy across methods. In one causal block, later phase slots can read earlier raw auxiliary-slot inputs but cannot read a contextualized earlier phase representation containing its context/history. The registered task requires that cross-slot path.
protocol_amendments.change: Use two causal slot blocks for all methods, matching the depth of the adjacent TM001 period decoder; retain P=4, methods, data, learning-rate candidates and 1,200-update budget. Preserve the initial development rows as architecture_v1; re-run development as architecture_v2 and use only v2 for selection and fresh evaluation.

protocol_amendments.stage: development only; no fresh worlds opened
protocol_amendments.reason: A methods audit found that the runner used method-specific minibatch streams, adding avoidable data-order noise to the control comparison.
protocol_amendments.change: Keep method-specific initialization seeds but use identical minibatch samples across all methods and learning rates within each world/mode. Retain two causal blocks, same task, learning-rate candidates, and update budget. Preserve v1 and v2 development rows; only the matched-minibatch v3 development run selects the rate and may open fresh worlds.
